title: Meridian execution run state
description: The complete schema for the state of ONE execution run (record_type: execution-run): a portable, storage-independent, human- and machine-readable snapshot of one actual attempt to carry out a task specification. A record declares THIS schema in its $schema, so a consumer that follows the declaration validates the whole record — the record envelope AND the specialised body — in one pass, and never accepts a body without id, scope, origin and authority. The record envelope is the SAME contract as registries/operating-model/scoped-record.schema.json (identity, scope, origin, authority): scripts/lib/execution-state.mjs validates every record against scoped-record.schema.json directly as well, so the canonical envelope check is reused and separately performed, never silently dropped. The managed entity is the RUN, not the conversational "task": one task specification may drive several runs, each with its own stable id and its own Russian title, and each references EXACTLY ONE task specification by a portable task_specification_ref — the specification is never absorbed or duplicated inside the payload. This schema narrows scope to the one workspace-scope-model area a run record may occupy — run-state (scope.id identifies the run, scope.workspace_id is mandatory); project-workspace, repository-scope, built-in-methodology, user-profile and organization-profile are rejected. The physical directory, the Instance repository and the storage mechanism are not the area. The payload carries the independent axes of the minimal current state — lifecycle_stage, work_status, scope_revision, current_actor, resolved_norms, completed_checks, blockers, next_action, next_gate and an ordered transition_history — as a CLOSED object, so one universal "status" field standing in for several axes is rejected by construction, and so is a leaked role, supervision mode, communication mode, context manifest or full evidence/handoff field that belongs to a later package. lifecycle_stage is the closed ordered pool intake → classification → norm_resolution → planning → execution → verification → acceptance → integration → deployment → observation → completion; work_status is the closed pool planned, ready, active, waiting_human, blocked, failed, completed, cancelled. next_action and next_gate are stated explicitly: a non-empty string, or an explicit null where there is no continuation — never a missing key. The rules this JSON Schema subset cannot state live in scripts/lib/execution-state.mjs: the declared $schema is RESOLVED as a LOGICAL address within the Meridian namespace and must resolve to exactly this file's logical address — not merely carry the right basename, and not the bare scoped-record envelope (resolution and the rooted-path rules are REUSED from scripts/lib/task-specification.mjs, no divergent copy); a non-empty blockers list agrees with work_status blocked and vice versa; waiting_human names a concrete next action; a completed or cancelled run carries no executable next step; blockers carry a stable id, a description and a verifiable resumption condition; resolved_norms and completed_checks are unique portable references; the transition history is ordered by an explicit strictly-increasing sequence whose ordinal never repeats or decreases, its first record states the initial state (from_stage and from_status null), each later record continues the previous state with no break, the last record matches the current lifecycle_stage, work_status and scope_revision, the per-transition scope_revision never decreases, a backward lifecycle move needs a backward_rationale, a skipped stage needs an explicit inapplicability basis, a transition after a terminal state needs a reopen_rationale, and every transition states a reason; portability of every reference string; the Russian name. The contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/execution-state-model.md.

next_step.description: An executable value (a non-empty string) or an explicit null where there is no continuation. The key is always required, so an absent axis is never read as null.

scope_ref.description: A run record's area. Only run-state is accepted; every other area of the workspace scope model is rejected here (and in scripts/lib/execution-state.mjs with the rationale). scope.id identifies the run; workspace_id ties the run to its project workspace (workspace-scope-model.md §1).

origin.description: Same contract as scoped-record.schema.json's origin. A run is started in a workspace, so kind 'built-in' is additionally rejected by scripts/lib/execution-state.mjs.

blocker.description: One structured blocker. id is a stable semantic identifier, unique within the run. description states the condition. resumption_condition is the observable condition under which continuation becomes possible again — not a free phrase. A non-empty blockers list agrees with work_status 'blocked' (checked in scripts/lib/execution-state.mjs); 'blocked' and 'waiting_human' are not interchangeable.

stage_skip.description: An explicit statement that a lifecycle stage does not apply and is deliberately not passed through. A transition that jumps over a stage without a matching stage_skip is rejected as a silent skip.

transition.description: One entry in the ordered transition history. sequence is the explicit ordinal (strictly increasing, never repeated or decreasing); it is the ordering, not object or file order. The first entry states the initial state: from_stage and from_status are null. Every later entry continues the previous entry's to_stage / to_status with no break, and the last entry matches the run's current lifecycle_stage, work_status and scope_revision. reason is mandatory. backward_rationale is required for a move to an earlier stage; skipped_stages is required to jump over a stage; reopen_rationale is required for any entry after a completed or cancelled state. The history stores run state, not a full command log or transcript.

payload.description: The independent axes of one run's minimal current state, as a CLOSED object. Every axis is required and no other field is accepted, so a single universal 'status' field, and role / supervision-mode / communication-mode / context-manifest / full-evidence fields that belong to later packages, are rejected by construction. next_action and next_gate are next_step: an action string or an explicit null.
